values.value: • Lead with the few capabilities that matter most to this buyer. • Translate capability fit into specific outcomes, implementation ease, and risk reduction. • Support the fit claim with relevant proof from similar B2B or academic cases. • Pre-empt objections on delivery, adoption, integration, or scale. • Now focus on buying path, not just product fit.
5|Yes
Buyer may say, 'Others also say they can do this.' Response: 'Fair point. Let me show you not just fit, but why our delivery and outcome path is stronger for your context.'
Good fit. Now translate capability into their language with a crisp before-after story and proof points.
Low risk. Move from fit to proof.
Say: 'Based on what you shared, this is how we solve it end to end and what outcome you should expect.'
Yes

• Do not hide the partial fit. Reframe the deal around the problems you solve best. • Check whether the missing 50% is truly critical or only desirable. • Offer a phased solution, partner path, or alternate delivery model if appropriate. • Protect trust by being explicit about what is in scope and what is not. • Only progress if the buyer agrees the important needs are covered.
5|Partially, about 50%
Buyer may say, 'Can you still cover the rest?' Response: 'Possibly through phasing or a different scope. I would rather be clear now and build the right path than over-promise.'
Do not oversell. Narrow the scope, position a phased approach, or combine services so the fit feels safe.
Risk: Overpromising will hurt trust later.
Ask: 'Would phase one on the top priorities make sense while we plan the remaining gaps?'
Partially, about 50%

• Do not oversell a weak fit just to keep the deal alive. • Challenge whether this opportunity should be pursued in its current shape. • Explore scope reset, pilot, adjacent use case, or partner-led route. • If the core requirement is a mismatch, qualify out early and professionally. • Save time for deals where you can genuinely win and deliver well.
5|Less than 30%
Buyer may say, 'Can you customise heavily?' Response: 'We can explore that, but first I want to be honest about whether this remains the right opportunity for both sides.'
Do not force-fit the deal. Re-qualify hard, reshape the problem, or walk away if the gap is too large.
High risk: Weak solution fit.
Say: 'I do not want to sell you the wrong setup. Let us first check if the core fit is strong enough.'
Less than 30%

• Run a structured fit-gap discussion with product, delivery, or solutioning support. • Map the buyer requirement against your actual capability, delivery readiness, and constraints. • Clarify integrations, services dependency, learner format, analytics need, and rollout model. • Avoid promising anything before internal validation is complete. • Then position the strongest viable path, not a hopeful one.
5|Don't know
Buyer may say, 'Can you confirm later?' Response: 'Yes, but I would like to validate internally first so whatever I commit is dependable.'
Map their requirements against your solution line by line before the next meeting. Certainty beats optimism here.
Risk: Unknown fit creates proposal rework.
Ask: 'Can we validate the top use cases together so I can confirm fit honestly?'
Don't know
Can our offerings / capability fulfil the customer's requirements fully?
